newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brokers mull foreign currency money funds.
newsitem.headline: Japan brokers mull foreign currency money funds.

text.p: New Japan Securities Co Ltd, Okasan Securities Co Ltd and Wako Securities Co Ltd are considering jointly starting foreign-currency denominated money management funds (MMFs), sources at the brokerage houses said on Tuesday.
"It is true that we may start such funds this year, but no final decision has been reached," a source at a brokerage house said.

If the three brokerages are able to reach an agreement, the foreign-currency denominated MMFs will likely invest mostly in foreign bonds with short maturities, and target retail investors suffering from low domestic interest rates who seek higher yields available in overseas markets, another brokerage source said.

"Foreign bonds sold very well to retail investors last year. Bonds, however, have relatively long maturities, and I think there may be a need for foreign-currency denominated financial products with shorter maturities," a market source said.
Sources said joint sales of the MMFs would help enlarge the size of the funds, which will help stabilise returns on investment.

"From the standpoint of investment, large fluctuations in the size of the funds are undesirable... By selling the funds together, the size of the funds would be larger than if it was done by one company and would help stabilise returns," the market source said.
The actual management of the fund is likely to be entrusted to a foreign banking subsidiary of the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, the sources said.
